transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I’ve been having trouble with elevators, mostly. Slow ones, or small locked rooms. Soon as I’m in there, my chest sort of jumps and I feel like I need to get out right away, before I can think much.
Do you feel this way only in elevators and small rooms, or does it also happen in other situations where you feel trapped or can’t easily get out?
Mostly places like that, yeah. Elevators, little rooms… if there’s no window and the door shuts tight, my mind kind of takes it as trouble, even if I know it’s just a storage room or something.
Do you ever feel sudden episodes of intense fear or discomfort that happen out of the blue, even when you’re not in those tight spaces?
No… I don’t think so. It’s usually when I’m in one of those places. Not just sitting around out of nowhere.
When you’re in an elevator or a small room, do you feel like you might panic or lose control, or are you more worried about something bad physically happening to you in there?

It’s more that my head treats it like something bad could happen, I guess. I know an elevator or a little storage room isn’t really the same as being locked up, but when there’s no window and the door shuts tight… it feels like trouble.
When you think about going into an elevator or a small room, do you worry more about having a panic attack or about something physically bad happening to you?

More like something bad happening, I suppose. I know a little room or elevator isn’t the same as being locked up, but once I see there’s no window and that door shuts tight… my mind just treats it like trouble.

Do you avoid elevators or small rooms because you’re worried something physically dangerous might happen in there, like getting stuck or not getting help, or is it more about how your body or mind might react once you’re inside?

I guess it’s more the place itself… being closed in. These days I usually take the stairs, or I’ll pass on those archive jobs at the museum. If I can’t avoid it, I might ask a friend to stay nearby. Feels a little foolish, but… it helps.
So when you're faced with going into an elevator or a small room, is your main concern that you might panic once you're in there, or is it more about the actual fact of being closed in?
It’s more the being closed in, I’d say. I know an elevator or little storage room isn’t really being locked up, but when there’s no window and the door shuts tight… my mind treats it like trouble.
When you think about being in an elevator or a small room, does your worry mostly come from feeling like you can’t escape or won’t get help, or is it more about the actual feeling of being enclosed?

It’s more the enclosed part, I think. I know a small storage room or elevator at the museum isn’t really being locked up, but when there’s no window and that door shuts tight… my mind just treats it like trouble.

When you think about being in a small room or elevator, is your main concern that you wouldn’t be able to get out easily or get help if needed, or is it more about the actual feeling of being enclosed, regardless of whether you could get out or not?

It’s more the closed-in feeling. I know a little storage room or an elevator isn’t really the same as being locked up, but once I see there’s no window and the door shuts tight… my mind treats it like trouble.

If you were in a small room or elevator but the door was left open or you knew you could leave anytime, would you still feel the same sense of trouble, or does it mostly happen when you feel like you can't get out easily?

If the door’s open, or I know I can step right out, it’s not the same. It’s mostly when there’s no window and the door shuts tight. Then… my mind treats it like trouble, even if I know it isn’t really.
